{{Short description|American statistician and defense acquisitions analyst}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=July 2021}}
'''Nancy Lyon Spruill''' is a retired American statistician and defense acquisitions analyst, formerly the director of Acquisition Resources and Analysis in the [[United States Department of Defense]].{{r|charts}} Within the Department of Defense, she is known for the "Spruill chart", a [[spreadsheet]] for estimating the costs of weapons programs that she developed,{{r|charts|cost}} and for threatening to sue the [[United States Navy]] in 1979 because it would not allow her, as a woman, to stay aboard one of its aircraft carriers.{{r|charts}} 

==Education and career==
Spruill is the daughter and granddaughter of federal workers.{{r|charts}} She is a 1971 graduate of the [[University of Maryland, College Park]],{{r|umd}} majoring in mathematics,{{r|distinguished}} and on graduating became a research assistant in the [[Center for Naval Analyses]].{{r|charts}} She earned a master's degree in 1975,{{r|distinguished}} and completed a Ph.D. in 1980 at [[George Washington University]], with the dissertation ''Two statistical problems involving the bivariate normal distribution arising from legal issues''.{{r|diss}} In 1983 she moved to the office of the Secretary of Defense, eventually becoming a senior [[operations research]] analyst there. In 1993 she moved to the [[Defense Mapping Agency]], and in 1999 she returned to the office of the secretary as director of acquisition resources and analysis.{{r|distinguished}} She retired in 2018.{{r|tribute}}

==Recognition==
In 2003, she was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} The American Statistical Association Section on Statistics in Defense and National Security gave her their Distinguished Achievement Award in 2006.{{r|distinguished}} She is also a recipient of the [[Department of Defense Distinguished Civilian Service Award]], the [[Secretary of Defense Exceptional Civilian Service Award]], the Hammer Award, the David D. Acker "Skill in Communication" Award, and the [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Award]].{{r|distinguished|tribute}}
